Done. The MFMA-based Conv2D kernel compiles and passes all 5 correctness trials.

**What the kernel does:**

- Implements Conv2D as an implicit GEMM: output channels (OC=64) map to the M dimension, output spatial positions (N×OH×OW) map to N, and the kernel flattened dimension (IC×KH×KW=1440) maps to K
- Uses `al.amdgpu.mfma_32x32x8_bf16_f32` with the correct per-thread register layout: 2×u32 packed A/B operands and 16×f32 accumulator, matching the MFMA swizzle invariants
- Threads are split into two groups of 32 across the K dimension: lanes 0–31 load K indices 0–3, lanes 32–63 load K indices 4–7, so all 8 K elements are covered per MFMA call
- Accumulates in FP32 and converts to BF16 at store time, following the standard MFMA writeback mapping

**Eval results:**

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Compiled | true |
| Correctness | 5/5 |
| Runtime | 33.3 ms |
| Ref runtime | 1.53 ms |

The runtime gap is expected — the optimization guidance explicitly prohibits LDS staging, vectorized loads, and async copies. Those are the main levers that would bring performance closer to cuDNN. The key deliverable was replacing scalar accumulation with MFMA, which is working correctly.
